profile.summary: Omni-DNA is a family of generative DNA language models, named by size from 20M to 1B parameters, that read a DNA sequence and predict the next token. After pretraining on multi-species genomes, a single model can be fine-tuned to answer several tasks at once, producing a class label, a text description of function, or image tokens from a DNA input. The base models can also be fine-tuned with a classification head like other genomic foundation models.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper abstract and Figure 4; README Capabilities; Hugging Face API

summary_quotes.text: a family of cross-modal multi-task models ranging from 20 million to 1 billion parameters
enables the model to perform diverse tasks including classification, function prediction, and DNA-to-image.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Omni-DNA works in two stages. First, decoder-only transformers based on OLMo are pretrained on DNA alone by next-token prediction. Then a model is fine-tuned on several tasks at once: the tokenizer vocabulary is expanded with new tokens for each task's outputs (class labels, text, or discrete image codes), and the model learns to generate the answer after the input sequence and a task description. To limit the shift in existing tokens caused by vocabulary expansion, the authors use a method they call Important Key Repetition together with NEFTune. Base models can also be fine-tuned in the usual way with a classification head.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Introduction, Figure 4, Section 3; README: Capabilities

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Six base sizes and three fine-tuned 1B models are released on Hugging Face. The 116M and 1B models use non-parametric layer norm and the other four use RMSNorm. The repository's run.sh lists the commands used to replicate the paper's experiments, including classification fine-tuning and inference with the multi-task, DNA-to-text and DNA-to-image models. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision; this page read Omni-DNA-1B at revision 0ea9d54e.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Family of autoregressive (decoder-only) DNA foundation models, pretrained by next-token prediction and then fine-tuned for classification, multi-task and cross-modal generation tasks.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Figure 4 caption; model card: Model Description

quotes.text: Omni-DNA are trained on DNA only with next-token prediction.
enables the model to perform diverse tasks including classification, function prediction, and DNA-to-image.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer decoder built on OLMo, with rotary position embeddings (RoPE), SwiGLU activation and a BPE tokenizer with an initial vocabulary of 4096. Base sizes run from 8 layers and hidden size 256 (20M) to 16 layers and hidden size 2048 (1B).
facts.source_locator: Paper Section 3; Omni-DNA-1B config.json; README: Base Models

quotes.text: We build on Open Language Model (OLMo)

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequences as text, tokenised by BPE; for fine-tuned models, a sequence followed by a task description, as in the SFT data format.
facts.source_locator: Model card: Usage; README: SFT Example

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Generated tokens (DNA, class labels, text or image tokens, depending on the fine-tuned model), or class logits when a classification head is attached.

quotes.text: We show Multi-tasking examples in `src/multitask_sft`, and dna2text examples in `src/dna_2_text`.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 10,490,112 (Omni-DNA-20M), 37,757,440 (60M), 116,391,936 (116M), 272,663,552 (300M), 616,613,376 (700M), 1,082,130,432 (1B); the fine-tuned Multitask, DNA2Function and DNA2Image models have 1,090,605,056, 1,107,222,528 and 1,090,547,712. All are safetensors counts from Hugging Face. Several counts differ from the size in the name (for example 10,490,112 for 20M and 37,757,440 for 60M); the sources do not explain this.
facts.source_locator: Hugging Face API safetensors field for each checkpoint

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: NCBI's multi-species genome dataset, reduced to 30 billion nucleotides after exact duplicates were removed. The models were trained on 300 billion nucleotides; the paper says multiple epochs can still be used after the reduction.
facts.source_locator: Paper Section 3 (pretraining, deduplication); README: Base Models

quotes.text: These model are trained on 300 billion nucleotides.
we removed exact duplicates from NCBI’s multi-species genome dataset
reducing it to 30 billion nucleotides. Despite this reduction, multiple epochs can still be used in training.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Six base models (Omni-DNA 20M, 60M, 116M, 300M, 700M and 1B) and three supervised fine-tuned models built on the 1B base (Omni-DNA-Multitask, Omni-DNA-DNA2Function, Omni-DNA-DNA2Image).

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: 2024, as the model card's Date cutoff field states. The card does not say what the date refers to.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 250 tokens for all base models (README, card and config max_sequence_length). The paper's hyperparameter table gives the sequence length as 250 tokens and says the context length can be extended during fine-tuning; the README's fine-tuning example sets a maximum of 1000 and the SFT example 512.
facts.source_locator: README tables and examples; config.json; paper Section 3, Appendix A

strengths.text: One fine-tuned model can handle several tasks and output types (classification labels, text and image tokens), instead of one fine-tuned model per task.

quotes.text: Unlike previous Genomic Foundation Models (GFMs), which require separate fine-tuning for each task, Omni-DNA leverages **auto-regressive transformer-based training** and **multi-task fine-tuning**, enabling a single model to perform a wide range of genomic tasks

strengths.text: A wide range of sizes, from 10,490,112 to 1,082,130,432 parameters for the base models, all MIT licensed and not gated.
The authors report that the autoregressive models match or outperform bidirectional transformers on genomic sequence modelling.

quotes.text: The auto-regressive model can match or outperform the bidirectional transformer on genomic sequence modeling.

limitations.text: The pretrained context is short, 250 tokens; longer inputs depend on extending the context during fine-tuning.

quotes.text: the context length of the pretrained model can still be easily extended during finetuning

limitations.text: The authors say their evaluation does not cover long-range interaction prediction or variant effect prediction, and that high-fidelity cross-modal translation remains open.

quotes.text: our evaluation does not encompass important genomic challenges like long-range interaction prediction
achieving high-fidelity cross-modality translation remains an open challenge

run_guide.summary: Install the dependencies, get the repository at a pinned commit, and run the multi-task model on the histone modification test sets used in the paper.
prerequisites: conda, to create a Python 3.10 environment.
A CUDA GPU: the inference code moves the model to 'cuda'. GPU memory needs are not stated.
Internet access to download zehui127/Omni-DNA-Multitask and the zehui127/Omni-DNA-dataset-nt-downstream-multitask dataset from Hugging Face. Weights are MIT licensed and not gated.

steps.title: Create the environment and install dependencies
steps.shell:
conda create -n omni_dna python=3.10 -y
conda activate omni_dna
pip install trl==0.13 transformers datasets datasets ai2-olmo

quotes.text: pip install trl==0.13 transformers datasets datasets ai2-olmo

steps.explanation: Two lines from the README's run.sh. The script loads the multi-task model and its test dataset from Hugging Face and evaluates it on ten histone modification tasks.

outputs: For each of the ten tasks, a header line and a dictionary of accuracy, F1, Matthews correlation, precision and recall, printed to the terminal, as the code in inference_sft.py does.
